einstellungen.text: You remember your dad's empty seat. But not all of it.
The old ticket is in your hand. From your very first show, when you were twelve.
"You weren't there, Dad. The seat was empty."
You can see it perfectly. Front row. All the parents there. Just one seat empty.
You've carried that picture for five years. To every performance. Every parents' night.
Your dad nods. He doesn't argue. He just takes out his phone. The tea goes cold.
First photo. Six-oh-five p.m. Front row, one empty seat.
He keeps scrolling. Six fifty-two. The final applause. Everyone is standing up.
All the way in the back, by the door. A man in a gray jacket. Clapping harder than anyone.
Your dad. Totally out of breath, his cap crooked. You never saw him back then.
"My bus broke down. So I ran all the way."
Both things are true. The empty seat at the start. And the man at the door at the end.
You tell him how alone you felt back then. And that you're really glad he was there.
Your dad says quietly, "I was late. And you still had to feel alone."
